```tsx
describe("the form Open an order (8.4)", () => {
  const filled = (over: Partial<OrderFormState> = {}): OrderFormState => ({
    ...emptyOrderForm(),
    message: "none",
    channel: "portal",
    kind: "tco_removal",
    memberState: "DE",
    authorityChoice: "bka",
    reference: "BKA-2026-1",
    links: ["https://korbat.example/p/1", "", "  https://korbat.example/p/2  "].join(String.fromCharCode(10)),
    sectionC: "no",
    ...over,
  });
  const form = (state: OrderFormState, over: Partial<Parameters<typeof OrderForm>[0]> = {}) =>
    html(<OrderForm me={{ homeState: "DE" }} form={state} messages={[message()]} busy={false} problem={null} duplicate={null} onChange={noop} onSubmit={noop} onOpenOrder={noop} {...over} />);

  test("Section C untouched is never sent: the form says no choice is made for you", () => {
    expect(orderRequest(filled({ sectionC: null }))).toEqual({ ok: false, problem: "Choose whether the author must not be told: no choice is made for you." });
  });

  test("a removal order: the register's name for the authority, the links one a line, the post kept from its author", () => {
    const sent = orderRequest(filled());
    expect(sent).toEqual({
      ok: true,
      request: {
        messageId: null,
        channel: "portal",
        kind: "tco_removal",
        memberState: "DE",
        authority: "Bundeskriminalamt (BKA)",
        reference: "BKA-2026-1",
        links: ["https://korbat.example/p/1", "https://korbat.example/p/2"],
        sectionC: false,
        emergency: false,
        withholdFromAuthor: true,
      },
    });
    // A message picked is the mailbox, and its id is sent; I cannot tell holds like a tick.
    const picked = orderRequest(filled({ message: MESSAGE, channel: null, sectionC: "unsure", authorityChoice: "other", otherAuthority: HOSTILE.script }));
    expect(picked.ok && picked.request).toMatchObject({ messageId: MESSAGE, channel: "mailbox", sectionC: true, withholdFromAuthor: true, authority: HOSTILE.script });
  });

  test("a DSA order: the withholding only when ticked or forced by Section C; an order to provide information takes no link", () => {
    const art9 = orderRequest(filled({ kind: "dsa_art9" }));
    expect(art9.ok && art9.request.withholdFromAuthor).toBe(false);
    const ticked = orderRequest(filled({ kind: "dsa_art9", withhold: true }));
    expect(ticked.ok && ticked.request.withholdFromAuthor).toBe(true);
    const silent = orderRequest(filled({ kind: "dsa_art9", sectionC: "yes" }));
    expect(silent.ok && silent.request).toMatchObject({ sectionC: true, withholdFromAuthor: true });
    const art10 = orderRequest(filled({ kind: "dsa_art10" }));
    expect(art10.ok && art10.request).toMatchObject({ links: [], withholdFromAuthor: false, emergency: false });
    // Nothing named and nothing to send: the schema refuses it.
    expect(orderRequest(filled({ links: "" })).ok).toBe(false);
  });

  test("nothing is preselected that decides anything; the home state is listed first; the message not listed warns that no deadline shows", () => {
    const empty = form(emptyOrderForm());
    expect(empty).not.toMatch(/checked=""/);
    expect(empty).toMatch(/<option value="" selected="">-<[/]option><option value="DE">Germany [(]DE[)]<[/]option>/);
    expect(text(empty)).toContain("The message is not listed");
    expect(text(empty)).not.toContain("The order is opened without a time of receipt");
    expect(text(form(emptyOrderForm("none")))).toContain("The order is opened without a time of receipt, so korbat cannot show its deadline. Act now, as if the hour were almost over.");
    expect(text(form(emptyOrderForm("none")))).toContain("How it arrived");
  });

  test("DSA Article 9: the withholding is ticked and locked while the author must not be told, or while nobody can tell; free when Section C is not set", () => {
    const box = (out: string) => out.match(/<input type="checkbox"[^>]*>/g) ?? [];
    for (const sectionC of ["yes", "unsure"] as const) {
      const locked = form(filled({ kind: "dsa_art9", sectionC }));
      expect(box(locked)).toEqual(['<input type="checkbox" disabled="" checked=""/>']);
      expect(text(locked)).toContain("An author who must not be told cannot be shown their post marked as removed.");
    }
    const free = form(filled({ kind: "dsa_art9", sectionC: "no" }));
    expect(box(free)).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(box(free)[0]).not.toContain("disabled");
    expect(box(free)[0]).not.toContain("checked");
    expect(text(free)).toContain("Tick it only if the order's text says the content must be kept from its author too.");
    // The removal order's own box is the emergency, never the withholding.
    expect(text(form(filled()))).toContain("The order says it is an emergency");
    expect(text(form(filled()))).not.toContain("Withheld from the author");
  });

  test("order_exists links to the order that stands", () => {
    const out = form(filled(), { duplicate: parseOrderId(ID) as OrderId, problem: "x" });
    expect(out).toContain(`href="/orders/${ID}"`);
    expect(text(out)).toContain("Open the order that is recorded");
  });
});

describe("an order's page (8.5, Task 2's blocks)", () => {
  const me = { homeState: "DE", contactPoint: "orders@korbat.example", role: "moderator" } as const;
  const page = (order: OrderView, over: Partial<Parameters<typeof OrderPage>[0]> = {}) =>
    html(
      <OrderPage
        order={order}
        me={me}
        now={START}
        messages={[message()]}
        busy={false}
        notice={null}
        error={null}
        reasons={{}}
        links=""
        onReason={noop}
        onCloseItem={noop}
        onLinks={noop}
        onAddLinks={noop}
        onRecord={noop}
        onCorrect={noop}
        {...over}
      />,
    );

  test("the clock comes first, under the kind; block 4 only while an item names a post that can be disabled", () => {
    const out = text(page(view()));
    expect(out.indexOf(clockLine({ ...view(), items: 1 }, START))).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(out.indexOf(clockLine({ ...view(), items: 1 }, START))).toBeLessThan(out.indexOf("As written in the order"));
    expect(out).not.toContain("Disable for an order");
    expect(out).not.toContain("Extension received");
    expect(text(page(view({ items: [item({ postId: POST_A })] })))).toContain("Disable for an order");
  });

  test("block 2: a removal order is checked against the register, the authority drawn as text, with the home state's entries", () => {
    const out = html(<CheckBlock order={view({ authority: HOSTILE.script })} me={me} />);
    expect(out).toContain(HOSTILE_ESCAPED.script);
    expect(text(out)).toContain(`Before you act, check the order against your offline copy of the Commission's register: is ${HOSTILE.script} listed for Germany, and does the address`);
    expect(text(out)).toContain("Bundeskriminalamt (BKA): Bundeskriminalamt (BKA), contact point TCO@bka.bund.de");
    expect(text(out)).toContain("If you are in doubt and the hour is running, give effect");
    const dsa = text(html(<CheckBlock order={view({ kind: "dsa_art9", clock: null })} me={me} />));
    expect(dsa).toContain("No register lists who may issue such an order.");
    expect(dsa).toContain("it is given effect only after the check is recorded");
    expect(text(html(<CheckBlock order={view({ kind: "dsa_art9", clock: null, verified: true })} me={me} />))).not.toContain("given effect only after the check");
  });

  test("block 3: each link as an outsider's words; an account's and a missing link's lines; closing an open item needs a reason", () => {
    const items = [item({ link: HOSTILE.url, linkKind: "account" }), item({ id: "1f7c8b7e-4d0a-4c7e-9b8a-2f6e1d0c9b8a", position: 2, linkKind: "other" })];
    const out = page(view({ items }));
    expect(out).toContain(HOSTILE.url);
    expect(out).not.toContain(`href="${HOSTILE.url}"`);
    expect(text(out)).toContain("This link names an account, not a post.");
    expect(text(out)).toContain("This link names nothing that korbat serves.");
    expect(out.match(/<button type="button" disabled="">Close this item without effect<[/]button>/g)).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(page(view({ items }), { reasons: { [ITEM]: "no_post" } }).match(/<button type="button">Close this item without effect<[/]button>/g)).toHaveLength(1);
    // A disabled item, and an order nobody may correct, offer no closing.
    expect(text(page(view({ items: [item({ disabledAt: t(30) })] })))).toContain(`Disabled at ${bothTimes(t(30))}`);
    expect(text(page(view({ items: [item({ disabledAt: t(30) })] })))).not.toContain("Close this item without effect");
    expect(text(page(view({ mayCorrect: null })))).not.toContain("Close this item without effect");
  });

  test("block 5: only the events the database would take now; each is confirmed by the key, with its ground or message chosen first", () => {
    const out = html(<EventsBlock order={view({ mayEvents: ["annex3_sent", "clarification_received", "hold_extended"] })} messages={[message()]} busy={false} onRecord={noop} />);
    expect(text(out)).toContain("Annex III sent: Confirm with your staff key");
    expect(text(out)).toContain("Clarification received: Confirm with your staff key");
    // Task 3: an admin's "Extension received", with the message it came in and the end the database would release at.
    expect(text(out)).toContain("Extension received: Confirm with your staff key");
    expect(text(out)).toContain(`The notice is then held ${ORDER_RULES.holdExtensionDays} days longer, once.`);
    expect(text(out)).toContain(ANNEX3_GROUND_LABELS.insufficient_information);
    expect(text(out)).toContain(`Received ${bothTimes(AT)}, Inbox`);
    expect(text(out)).not.toContain("Close without effect");
    expect(out.match(/<button type="button" disabled="">/g)).toHaveLength(3);
    expect(html(<EventsBlock order={view({ mayEvents: [] })} messages={[]} busy={false} onRecord={noop} />)).toBe("");
  });

  test("block 6: the forms' values as text, the time in UTC with its offset, the contact point and the copy from the home state's facts", () => {
    expect(utcWithOffset("2026-10-10T01:00:12.345Z")).toBe("2026-10-10 01:00:12 +00:00");
    const stopped = view({ clock: { ...summary().clock!, stopped: true, stoppedAt: t(10), stopGround: "manifest_error" } });
    const out = text(html(<FormsBlock order={stopped} me={me} />));
    expect(out).toContain("Reference of the removal order: BKA-2026-1");
    expect(out).toContain("Issuing authority: Bundeskriminalamt (BKA), Germany (DE)");
    expect(out).toContain("Time and date of receipt of removal order: 2026-10-16 02:00:00 +00:00");
    expect(out).toContain(`Reason: ${ANNEX3_GROUND_LABELS.manifest_error}`);
    expect(out).toContain("Contact point: orders@korbat.example");
    expect(out).toContain("Copy to: TCO@bka.bund.de");
    expect(text(html(<FormsBlock order={view()} me={{ homeState: null, contactPoint: null }} />))).toContain("Contact point: not filled in: see the README, Before going public");
    expect(html(<FormsBlock order={view({ kind: "dsa_art9", clock: null })} me={me} />)).toBe("");
  });

  test("block 7: what the command line owes, one line each; nothing owed, no block", () => {
    const out = text(html(<OwedBlock order={view()} />));
    expect(out).toContain("The check is not recorded (staff.js order-verify).");
    expect(out).toContain("The order's own date and time are not recorded (staff.js order-issued).");
    expect(out).toContain("The authority's reasons and remedies are not recorded (staff.js order-texts).");
    expect(out).toContain("The document's digest is not recorded (staff.js order-document).");
    const none = { received: false, verification: false, issuedAt: false, texts: false, document: false, holdUntil: false, tellPerson: false, scrutinyUntil: null };
    expect(html(<OwedBlock order={view({ owed: none })} />)).toBe("");
    const dsa = text(html(<OwedBlock order={view({ kind: "dsa_art9", clock: null, owed: { ...none, texts: true } })} />));
    expect(dsa).toContain("Record the authority's reasons, its remedies and the order's territorial scope before you give effect");
  });

  test("block 8: told at the effect, or held: with no end, until the computed end, released", () => {
    expect(text(html(<NoticeBlock order={view({ items: [item({ disabledAt: t(30) })] })} />))).toContain(`Told at ${bothTimes(t(30))}.`);
    const hold = { until: null, basis: "regulation", open: true, extended: false, endedAt: null, endReason: null, releasedAt: null, noticesHeld: 1 } as const;
    expect(text(html(<NoticeBlock order={view({ sectionC: true, hold })} />))).toContain("Held with no end");
    const until = text(html(<NoticeBlock order={view({ sectionC: true, hold: { ...hold, open: false, until: t(60_000), releasedAt: t(60_000) } })} />));
    expect(until).toContain(`Held until ${bothTimes(t(60_000))}: the end the database computes from the Regulation's six weeks, counted from the receipt.`);
    expect(until).toContain(`Released at ${bothTimes(t(60_000))}.`);
    expect(html(<NoticeBlock order={view()} />)).toBe("");
  });

  test("block 9: the events newest first, each with who wrote it, a handle as text", () => {
    const events: OrderView["events"] = [
      { id: "9e6b7a6d-3c9f-4b6d-8a7f-1e5d0c9b8a7f", kind: "opened", ground: null, at: AT, effectiveAt: null, itemId: null, by: HOSTILE.script, via: "console" },
      { id: "0a7c8b7e-4d0a-4c7e-9b8a-2f6e1d0c9b8b", kind: "annex3_sent", ground: "force_majeure", at: t(10), effectiveAt: null, itemId: null, by: null, via: "cli" },
    ];
    const out = html(<EventsList order={view({ events })} />);
    expect(out).toContain(HOSTILE_ESCAPED.script);
    const read = text(out);
    expect(read.indexOf(`${bothTimes(t(10))}: Annex III sent: ${ANNEX3_GROUND_LABELS.force_majeure}`)).toBeLessThan(read.indexOf(`${bothTimes(AT)}: Order opened`));
    expect(read).toContain("command line");
    expect(read).toContain(`@${HOSTILE.script}, console`);
  });

  test("block 10: the rule decides the controls; a correction sends what changes and nothing else", () => {
    expect(html(<CorrectBlock order={view({ mayCorrect: null })} busy={false} onCorrect={noop} />)).toBe("");
    const caution = text(html(<CorrectBlock order={view({ mayCorrect: "caution" })} busy={false} onCorrect={noop} />));
    expect(caution).toContain("Section C is ticked: the author must not be told");
    expect(caution).not.toContain("Issuing state");
    expect(html(<CorrectBlock order={view({ mayCorrect: "caution", sectionC: true })} busy={false} onCorrect={noop} />)).toBe("");
    const entry = html(<CorrectBlock order={view()} busy={false} onCorrect={noop} />);
    expect(entry).toMatch(/<button type="button" disabled="">Correct<[/]button>/);
    // An order opened from a message keeps its channel: the field is offered only without one.
    expect(text(entry)).not.toContain("How it arrived");
    expect(text(html(<CorrectBlock order={view({ messageId: null, channel: "portal" })} busy={false} onCorrect={noop} />))).toContain("How it arrived");
    expect(text(html(<CorrectBlock order={view({ mayCorrect: "admin" })} busy={false} onCorrect={noop} />))).toContain("Correct: Confirm with your staff key");
    const order = view();
    const same = { kind: order.kind, memberState: order.memberState, authority: order.authority, reference: order.reference, channel: order.channel, sectionC: order.sectionC, emergency: order.emergency, withholdFromAuthor: order.withholdFromAuthor };
    expect(changedFacts(order, same)).toEqual({});
    expect(changedFacts(order, { ...same, reference: "BKA-2026-2", channel: "post" })).toEqual({ reference: "BKA-2026-2" });
    expect(changedFacts(view({ messageId: null }), { ...same, channel: "post" })).toEqual({ channel: "post" });
  });
});

describe("block 4, Disable for an order (8.5, Task 3)", () => {
  const ids = ["1a000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001", "1a000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002", "1a000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003"];
  const posts = [POST_C, POST_A, POST_B];
  const three = () => ids.map((id, i) => item({ id, position: i + 1, postId: posts[i]!, link: `https://korbat.example/p/${i + 1}` }));
  const block = (order: OrderView, over: Partial<Parameters<typeof EffectBlock>[0]> = {}) =>
    html(<EffectBlock order={order} role="moderator" ticks={{}} urgent={false} busy={false} effected={null} onUrgent={noop} onEffect={noop} {...over} />);
  const me = { homeState: "DE", contactPoint: "orders@korbat.example", role: "moderator" } as const;
  const page = (order: OrderView, over: Partial<Parameters<typeof OrderPage>[0]> = {}) =>
    html(
      <OrderPage
        order={order}
        me={me}
        now={START}
        messages={[]}
        busy={false}
        notice={null}
        error={null}
        reasons={{}}
        links=""
        onReason={noop}
        onCloseItem={noop}
        onLinks={noop}
        onAddLinks={noop}
        onRecord={noop}
        onCorrect={noop}
        {...over}
      />,
    );

  test("three items with one key: the params bind the order's facts and each ticked item, sorted by post; the lines of a told removal order", () => {
    const order = view({ items: three() });
    const out = text(block(order));
    expect(out).toContain("Disable 3 posts: confirm with your staff key");
    for (const line of [ORDER_WORDS.order.effectWhat, ORDER_WORDS.order.effectPreserve, ORDER_WORDS.order.effectTold, ORDER_WORDS.order.effectAnyone]) expect(out).toContain(line);
    expect(out).toContain("preserved for six months from now");
    expect(out).not.toContain(ORDER_WORDS.order.effectRemoved);
    const params = effectParamsOf(order, ids, false);
    expect(params).toEqual({
      kind: "tco_removal",
      memberState: "DE",
      authority: order.authority,
      reference: order.reference,
      sectionC: false,
      emergency: false,
      withholdFromAuthor: true,
      urgent: false,
      items: [
        { itemId: ids[1], postId: POST_A },
        { itemId: ids[2], postId: POST_B },
        { itemId: ids[0], postId: POST_C },
      ],
    });
    // The params are what the contract takes: one hash for one action.
    expect(OrderEffectedParams.safeParse(params).success).toBe(true);
    // An item unticked by the person leaves the params; one in force or closed is never offered.
    expect(isTicked(order, { [ids[0]!]: false }, ids[0]!)).toBe(false);
    expect(effectable(view({ items: [item({ postId: POST_A, inForce: true }), item({ id: ids[1]!, postId: POST_B, closedAt: AT, closedReason: "not_named" })] }))).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("more than itemsPerAction items: the first ten are ticked, [effect.max] says so; the button counts the ticks", () => {
    const many = Array.from({ length: ORDER_RULES.itemsPerAction + 2 }, (_, i) =>
      item({ id: `2b000000-0000-4000-8000-${String(i).padStart(12, "0")}`, position: i + 1, postId: `3c000000-0000-4000-8000-${String(i).padStart(12, "0")}` }),
    );
    const out = text(block(view({ items: many })));
    expect(out).toContain(ORDER_WORDS.order.effectMax);
    expect(out).toContain(`Disable ${ORDER_RULES.itemsPerAction} posts: confirm with your staff key`);
    // Ticking an eleventh greys the button: the database takes ten an action.
    const over = block(view({ items: many }), { ticks: { [many[ORDER_RULES.itemsPerAction]!.id]: true } });
    expect(over).toMatch(/<button type="button" disabled="">Disable 11 posts/);
  });

  test("the silence: a removal order with Section C is held until the computed end; a DSA order's until the authority's time, or with no end", () => {
    const hold = { until: t(60_000), basis: "regulation", open: false, extended: false, endedAt: null, endReason: null, releasedAt: null, noticesHeld: 0 } as const;
    const held = text(block(view({ items: three(), sectionC: true, hold })));
    expect(held).toContain(ORDER_WORDS.order.effectHeld(bothTimes(t(60_000))));
    expect(held).not.toContain(ORDER_WORDS.order.effectTold);
    const dsa = { kind: "dsa_art9", clock: null, verified: true, preserve: false } as const;
    const dsaHeld = text(block(view({ ...dsa, items: three(), withholdFromAuthor: true, hold: { ...hold, basis: "authority" } })));
    expect(dsaHeld).toContain(ORDER_WORDS.order.effectHeldDsa(bothTimes(t(60_000))));
    expect(dsaHeld).not.toContain(ORDER_WORDS.order.effectPreserve);
    expect(text(block(view({ ...dsa, items: three(), withholdFromAuthor: true, hold: { ...hold, basis: "authority", open: true, until: null } })))).toContain(ORDER_WORDS.order.effectHeldOpen);
    // A DSA order that does not withhold removes, as a korbat rule does, and tells the author.
    const removed = text(block(view({ ...dsa, items: three(), withholdFromAuthor: false })));
    expect(removed).toContain(ORDER_WORDS.order.effectRemoved);
    expect(removed).toContain(ORDER_WORDS.order.effectTold);
    expect(removed).not.toContain(ORDER_WORDS.order.effectWhat);
  });

  test("a DSA Article 9 order that is not verified: no button for a moderator; an admin ticks urgent first, and the params carry it", () => {
    const order = view({ kind: "dsa_art9", clock: null, verified: false, preserve: false, items: three() });
    const moderator = text(block(order));
    expect(moderator).toContain(ORDER_WORDS.order.verifyFirst);
    expect(moderator).not.toContain("confirm with your staff key");
    const admin = block(order, { role: "admin" });
    expect(text(admin)).toContain(ORDER_WORDS.order.effectUrgent);
    expect(admin).toMatch(/<button type="button" disabled="">Disable 3 posts/);
    expect(block(order, { role: "admin", urgent: true })).toMatch(/<button type="button">Disable 3 posts/);
    expect(effectParamsOf(order, ids, true).urgent).toBe(true);
  });

  test("after an effect: the check from outside, each address as text; [effect.rest] while items are open; an item's preservation, reinstatement and case", () => {
    const disabled = item({ id: ids[0]!, postId: POST_A, link: HOSTILE.script, inForce: true, disabledAt: t(20), caseId: CASE, decisionId: CASE, preserveUntil: t(300_000) });
    const order = view({ items: [disabled, item({ id: ids[1]!, position: 2, postId: POST_B })], clock: { ...summary().clock!, itemsOpen: 1, firstEffectAt: t(20) } });
    const out = block(order, { effected: { at: t(20), links: [HOSTILE.script] } });
    expect(text(out)).toContain(ORDER_WORDS.order.checkOutside(bothTimes(t(20)), 1));
    expect(out).toContain(HOSTILE_ESCAPED.script);
    expect(out).not.toContain("<a");
    expect(text(out)).toContain(ORDER_WORDS.order.effectRest(1, bothTimes(t(60))));
    const read = page(order, { onOpenCase: noop });
    expect(text(read)).toContain(`Preserved until ${bothTimes(t(300_000))}`);
    expect(read).toContain(`href="/cases/${CASE}"`);
```

import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import { ALERT_RULES, ALERT_TEXTS, EDGE_CACHE, EDGE_RULES, ORDER_RULES, REPLY_AIM_HOURS, RETENTION, STANDING_RULES } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { AUTOMATION_WORDS } from "../src/messages";
import { ERASURE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK, RELEASE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK } from "../src/screens/Home";

/**
 * The README's moderation runbook and the console's home screen say the same thing (3c design, section 13, Task 12).
 * When decided items wait for the daily release longer than it ever takes, or an erasure is more than a day late, the
 * home screen shows the count with the runbook's sentence for it, and each sentence is a constant of the screen. This
 * test reads README.md from the repository's root and holds the runbook to the same two constants, word for word, so
 * that what staff are told on the screen is what the operator reads in the runbook: whoever changes one changes both.
 */
const README = path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, "..", "..", "..", "README.md");

/** Markdown's code mark. The README sets a log line or a setting in code marks; the console shows the same words as plain text. */
const CODE_MARK = "`";

/** A text as its reader sees it: without the code marks. Nothing else is changed, so every word and every sign must agree. */
const withoutCodeMarks = (text: string): string => text.split(CODE_MARK).join("");

/** The README's lines, as written. */
function readmeLines(): string[] {
  return readFileSync(README, "utf8").split("\n");
}

/** The lines of the README's section "Moderation": from its heading to the next heading of the same level. */
function moderationSection(): string[] {
  const lines = readmeLines();
  const start = lines.indexOf("## Moderation");
  if (start === -1) return [];
  const rest = lines.slice(start + 1);
  const end = rest.findIndex((line) => line.startsWith("## "));
  return end === -1 ? rest : rest.slice(0, end);
}

/** The section's runbook as its reader sees it: every line after "The runbook:", without the code marks. */
function moderationRunbook(): string {
  const section = moderationSection();
  const start = section.indexOf("The runbook:");
  return start === -1 ? "" : withoutCodeMarks(section.slice(start + 1).join("\n"));
}

/** How often `part` stands in `text`. */
const count = (text: string, part: string): number => text.split(part).length - 1;

describe("the README's moderation runbook says what the home screen says", () => {
  const sentences: [string, string][] = [
    ["decisions not released", RELEASE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK],
    ["late erasures", ERASURE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK],
  ];

  test("the README has a section Moderation, and the section has a runbook", () => {
    expect(readmeLines()).toContain("## Moderation");
    expect(moderationSection()).toContain("The runbook:");
    expect(moderationRunbook().trim()).not.toBe("");
  });

  test("neither constant holds a code mark or a line break, so reading the README without its code marks hides no difference", () => {
    for (const [name, sentence] of sentences) {
      expect(sentence, name).not.toContain(CODE_MARK);
      expect(sentence, name).not.toContain("\n");
      // A whole sentence: it opens with "A count of" and ends in a full stop, as the runbook's bullet writes it.
      expect(sentence.startsWith("A count of "), name).toBe(true);
      expect(sentence.endsWith("."), name).toBe(true);
    }
  });

  for (const [name, sentence] of sentences) {
    test(`the runbook holds the home screen's sentence for ${name}, word for word`, () => {
      expect(moderationRunbook()).toContain(sentence);
    });

    test(`the sentence for ${name} stands once in the README, in that runbook: no second copy can drift from it`, () => {
      expect(count(withoutCodeMarks(readmeLines().join("\n")), sentence)).toBe(1);
      expect(count(moderationRunbook(), sentence)).toBe(1);
    });
  }

  test("both sentences stand in one bullet of the runbook, the release's first, as the home screen orders its two lines", () => {
    const bullets = moderationRunbook()
      .split("\n")
      .filter((line) => line.includes(RELEASE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK) || line.includes(ERASURE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK));
    expect(bullets).toHaveLength(1);
    const bullet = bullets[0] ?? "";
    expect(bullet.startsWith("- ")).toBe(true);
    expect(bullet.indexOf(RELEASE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK)).toBeGreaterThan(-1);
    expect(bullet.indexOf(ERASURE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK)).toBeGreaterThan(bullet.indexOf(RELEASE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK));
  });
});

/**
 * The README's account sanctions (3e design, section 13, Task 7) and the constants they print. The section Moderation
 * describes 3e in a paragraph that opens with ACCOUNT_SANCTIONS_LEAD and a bullet for each title below, and its runbook
 * gains the bullets of section 13's (a) to (h). Every number in that text is a number of STANDING_RULES or

const ACCOUNT_SANCTIONS_LEAD = "Account sanctions (sub-project 3e;";

/** The lines of 3e's text in Moderation, without code marks: the lead paragraph and each bullet by its bold title. */

describe("the README's account sanctions say what the constants say (3e design, section 13, Task 7)", () => {
  test("Moderation opens 3e's part with its paragraph, and each of its bullets stands there once", () => {

/**
 * The README's authorities' orders (3f design, section 13, Task 7; W.9 and W.10) and the constants they print. 3f's text
 * is the section "Authorities' orders", Upgrading from its 3f paragraph on (Task 1), Restoring's block "Restoring with
 * the keeper's copy" (Task 6) and Before going public's owner's list. Every number in it is a number of ORDER_RULES or
 * ALERT_RULES: a table holds each in its sentence, and every other run of digits is refused but for what names a
 * reference (an article, a research finding, a row of the design's section 2, a check P1 to P8, a list's numbering, a
 * path, a date), so the README cannot keep a number the constants changed. A setting is written as the operator sets it
 * in infra/.env, an API setting with the prefix Compose maps. A section added to 3f's text joins its list here.
 */
const FENCE = "```";

/** The lines of a "## " section of the README, from its heading to the next heading of the same level. */
function sectionLines(heading: string): string[] {
  const lines = readmeLines();
  const start = lines.indexOf(heading);
  if (start === -1) return [];
  const rest = lines.slice(start + 1);
  const end = rest.findIndex((line) => line.startsWith("## "));
  return end === -1 ? rest : rest.slice(0, end);
}
/** A section's lines from the first that begins with these words to the section's end, or to the first that begins with `until`. */
function linesFrom(lines: string[], lead: string, until?: string): string[] {
  const start = lines.findIndex((line) => line.startsWith(lead));
  if (start === -1) return [];
  const rest = lines.slice(start);
  const end = until === undefined ? -1 : rest.findIndex((line) => line.startsWith(until));
  return end === -1 ? rest : rest.slice(0, end);
}
/** Lines without their fenced code: a command's own numbers and words are not the runbook's. */
function withoutFences(lines: string[]): string[] {
  let inside = false;
  return lines.filter((line) => {
    if (line.startsWith(FENCE)) {
      inside = !inside;
      return false;
    }
    return !inside;
  });
}

const ORDERS_HEADING = "## Authorities' orders";
const ORDERS_TITLES = [
  "The contact point.",
  "On call.",
  "A removal order, step by step",
  "Other messages and orders.",
  "When nobody can act within the hour.",
  "Notifications and hand-overs.",
  "A person asks about a missing post.",
  "An author writes about an order's notice.",
  "The daily copy.",
  "A key in someone else's hands.",
  "The yearly counts.",
] as const;
const OWNERS_LEAD = "**The owner's list (sub-project 3f).**";
const OWNERS_TITLES = [
  "The Member State.",
  "The mailbox.",
  "The people's own access to the mailbox.",
  "Registering.",
  "The push hostname and ntfy's users.",
  "The phones.",
  "The keys.",
  "The papers, and counsel.",
  "The contact address.",
  "The page for the yearly report.",
  "The keeper, and the two places files rest.",
  "Decide",
  "Counsel",
] as const;

/** 3f's text, part by part, without code marks and fenced code. */
function ordersParts(): Record<"orders" | "upgrading" | "restoring" | "owners", string> {
  const read = (lines: string[]) => withoutCodeMarks(withoutFences(lines).join("\n"));
  return {
    orders: read(sectionLines(ORDERS_HEADING)),
    upgrading: read(linesFrom(sectionLines("## Upgrading"), "Authorities' orders and the alert channel (sub-project 3f)")),
    restoring: read(linesFrom(sectionLines("## Restoring"), "**Restoring with the keeper's copy**")),
    owners: read(linesFrom(sectionLines("## Before going public"), OWNERS_LEAD, "Set these in")),
  };
}
const ordersText = (): string => Object.values(ordersParts()).join("\n");

/** A number in a sentence as the README writes it, and the constant it is. */
const O = ORDER_RULES;
const A = ALERT_RULES;
const ORDER_NUMBERS: { constant: string; part: keyof ReturnType<typeof ordersParts>; phrase: string }[] = [
  { constant: "ALERT_RULES.pollSeconds", part: "orders", phrase: `reads the inbox and the junk folder every ${A.pollSeconds} seconds` },
  { constant: "ORDER_RULES.escalateMinutes", part: "orders", phrase: `it rings every staff phone ${O.escalateMinutes} minutes after its arrival` },
  { constant: "ORDER_RULES.itemsPerAction", part: "orders", phrase: `one key touch for up to ${O.itemsPerAction} posts` },
  { constant: "ORDER_RULES.holdWarningDays", part: "orders", phrase: `alerted daily in the last ${O.holdWarningDays} days before any release` },
  { constant: "ORDER_RULES.reportHoldDays", part: "orders", phrase: `the address is kept for at most ${O.reportHoldDays} days` },
  { constant: "ORDER_RULES.reportHoldDays", part: "upgrading", phrase: `keeps its address, and nothing else, for at most ${O.reportHoldDays} days` },
  { constant: "ORDER_RULES.copyOverdueHours", part: "orders", phrase: `once the newest copy is more than ${O.copyOverdueHours} hours old` },
  { constant: "ORDER_RULES.quietMinutes", part: "owners", phrase: `bounded only by the quiet period of ${O.quietMinutes} minutes` },
];

/** What names a reference and is no number of the runbook's, taken out before the digits are counted; only the second keeps a group, the character before the name. */
const REFERENCES: RegExp[] = [
  // A path, a file or a regulation's number: whatever holds a slash.
  /[A-Za-z0-9_.()-]*[/][A-Za-z0-9_./-]+/g,
  // A sub-project's name (3f, 3d, 1b) and a phone check (P1 to P8).
  /(^|[^0-9A-Za-z])([0-9][a-f]|P[1-8])(?=[^0-9A-Za-z]|$)/gm,
  // A list's numbering.
  /^[0-9]+[.] /gm,
  // An article of an act, with its paragraphs.
  /Art(?:icle|[.]) [0-9]+(?:[(][0-9a-z]+[)])*/g,
  // A finding of the research, with its questions; a row of the design's section 2, and the section itself.
  /(?:OL|AU) E[0-9]+[.][0-9]+(?: questions [0-9]+ to [0-9]+)?/g,
  /[(]rows? [0-9]+(?: and [0-9]+)?[)]/g,
  /section [0-9]+/g,
  // A step of a list named in a sentence.
  /steps? [0-9]+/g,
  // An instant as an example of the form, a date of the year, the hand-over's user, a hash's name, a status's code.
  /[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:]+Z/g,
  /[0-9]+ March/g,
  /uid [0-9]+/g,
  /sha256/g,
  /answers 503/g,
];

describe("the README's authorities' orders say what the constants say (3f design, section 13, Task 7; W.9 and W.10)", () => {
  test("the README has the section Authorities' orders after Moderation, and each of its parts stands there once, in W.9's order", () => {
    const lines = readmeLines();
    expect(lines.indexOf(ORDERS_HEADING)).toBeGreaterThan(lines.indexOf("## Moderation"));
    const section = sectionLines(ORDERS_HEADING).map(withoutCodeMarks);
    const at = ORDERS_TITLES.map((title) => section.findIndex((line) => line.startsWith(`**${title}`)));
    for (const title of ORDERS_TITLES) expect(section.filter((line) => line.startsWith(`**${title}`)), title).toHaveLength(1);
    expect([...at].sort((a, b) => a - b)).toEqual(at);
  });

  test("Before going public holds the owner's list of thirteen, each line by its title, in W.10's order", () => {
    const owners = linesFrom(sectionLines("## Before going public"), OWNERS_LEAD, "Set these in").filter((line) => /^[0-9]+[.] /.test(line));
    expect(owners.map((line) => line.slice(0, line.indexOf(" ")))).toEqual(OWNERS_TITLES.map((_, n) => `${n + 1}.`));
    for (const [n, title] of OWNERS_TITLES.entries()) expect(owners[n]!.startsWith(`${n + 1}. **${title}`), title).toBe(true);
  });

  test("every number of 3f's text stands in its sentence with the constant's value", () => {
    const parts = ordersParts();
    for (const row of ORDER_NUMBERS) expect(parts[row.part], `${row.constant}: ${row.phrase}`).toContain(row.phrase);
  });

  test("and no other number: every run of digits in it is a constant's, outside what names a reference", () => {
    const values = new Set<string>([...Object.values(O), ...Object.values(A)].filter((value) => typeof value === "number").map(String));
    const outside = REFERENCES.reduce((text, pattern) => text.replace(pattern, (_match: string, lead: unknown) => (typeof lead === "string" ? `${lead} ` : " ")), ordersText());
    expect((outside.match(/[0-9]+/g) ?? []).filter((digits) => !values.has(digits))).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("a setting is written as the operator sets it in infra/.env: an API setting with its prefix", () => {
    const withMarks = [sectionLines(ORDERS_HEADING), linesFrom(sectionLines("## Upgrading"), "Authorities' orders and the alert channel"), linesFrom(sectionLines("## Restoring"), "**Restoring with the keeper's copy**")]
      .flatMap((lines) => withoutFences(lines))
      .join("\n");
    for (const name of ["NOTIFY", "REPORT_HOLD", "MODERATION_RETENTION", "HOME_STATE", "CONTACT_POINT", "PUSH_ORIGIN", "APP_ORIGIN"]) {
      expect(withMarks.includes(`${CODE_MARK}${name}`), name).toBe(false);
    }
    for (const name of ["API_CONTACT_POINT", "API_HOME_STATE", "API_REPORT_HOLD", "API_MODERATION_RETENTION", "APP_SITE", "COMPOSE_PROFILES", "WEB_CONTACT_POINT", "WEB_HOME_STATE"]) {
      expect(withMarks.includes(name) || ordersText().includes(name), name).toBe(true);
    }
  });

  test("the hand-over's and the yearly counts' commands stand in the runbook as the operator types them", () => {
    const orders = ordersParts().orders;
    for (const words of [
      "docker compose --profile handover run --rm -T -v <directory>:/handover handover < list > digests",
      "handover-list",
      "handover-record",
      "handover-destroyed",

### Replace `apps/api/test/architecture.test.ts` (whole file)

```ts
import { readdirSync, readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { join, posix, relative, sep } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";

/**
 * Module boundaries (1a spec section 2.2, 2a spec section 2.2, 3a design section 5, 3c design section 5). Paths are relative to apps/api/src
 * with forward slashes. The rules are plain functions so the tests below can prove each one catches
 * a deliberate violation.
 */
interface SourceFile {
  path: string;
  source: string;
}

const SRC_ROOT = fileURLToPath(new URL("../src", import.meta.url));
const SCHEMA_ROOT = fileURLToPath(new URL("../../../packages/db/src/schema", import.meta.url));

/** Schema files that define auth-schema objects or shared helpers; every other schema file is public. */
const NON_PUBLIC_SCHEMA_FILES = new Set(["auth.ts", "helpers.ts", "index.ts"]);
const AUTH_SCHEMA_FILE = "auth.ts";
// The command lines open both pools: grant-role changes a role on the auth pool, and staff.js reads there the staff keys
// that audit-verify checks the record against.
const AUTH_POOL_ALLOWED = new Set(["config.ts", "index.ts", "cli/grant-role.ts", "cli/staff.ts"]);
const AUTH_KEYS_ALLOWED = new Set(["config.ts"]);

/** Modules that may only be entered through their index file. */
const MODULES = ["auth", "social", "media", "account", "staff", "moderation"] as const;

function walk(dir: string): string[] {
  return readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true }).flatMap((entry) => {
    const full = join(dir, entry.name);
    if (entry.isDirectory()) return walk(full);
    return entry.name.endsWith(".ts") ? [full] : [];
  });
}

function loadSources(): SourceFile[] {
  return walk(SRC_ROOT).map((full) => ({ path: relative(SRC_ROOT, full).split(sep).join("/"), source: readFileSync(full, "utf8") }));
}

function exportedNames(file: string): string[] {
  const source = readFileSync(join(SCHEMA_ROOT, file), "utf8");
  return [...source.matchAll(/^export (?:const|function|type|interface|enum) ([A-Za-z0-9_]+)/gm)].map((m) => m[1]!);
}

/** Names exported by the public-schema files of @korbat/db (tables and enums the auth module must not touch). */
function publicSchemaNames(): Set<string> {
  const names = new Set<string>();
  for (const file of readdirSync(SCHEMA_ROOT)) {
    if (!file.endsWith(".ts") || NON_PUBLIC_SCHEMA_FILES.has(file)) continue;
    for (const name of exportedNames(file)) names.add(name);
  }
  return names;
}

/** Names exported by the auth-schema file of @korbat/db (tables and enums the social module must not touch). */
function authSchemaNames(): Set<string> {
  return new Set(exportedNames(AUTH_SCHEMA_FILE));
}

/** Every module specifier in static imports, re-exports, side-effect imports and dynamic imports. */
function specifiers(source: string): string[] {
  return [...source.matchAll(/(?:\bfrom\s+|\bimport\s*\(\s*|\bimport\s+)["']([^"']+)["']/g)].map((m) => m[1]!);
}

/** Named bindings of every `import { ... } from "@korbat/db"`; a namespace import yields the marker "*". */
function dbImports(source: string): string[] {
  const names: string[] = [];
  for (const match of source.matchAll(/\bimport\s+(type\s+)?(\*\s+as\s+\w+|\{[^}]*\})\s+from\s+["'](@korbat\/db(?:\/[^"']*)?)["']/g)) {
    const bindings = match[2]!;
    if (bindings.startsWith("*")) {
      names.push("*");
      continue;
    }
    for (const part of bindings.slice(1, -1).split(",")) {
      const name = part.trim().replace(/^type\s+/, "").split(/\s+as\s+/)[0]!.trim();
      if (name) names.push(name);
    }
  }
  return names;
}

const insideAuth = (path: string) => path.startsWith("auth/");
const insideSocial = (path: string) => path.startsWith("social/");
const insideMedia = (path: string) => path.startsWith("media/");
const insideAccount = (path: string) => path.startsWith("account/");
const insideStaff = (path: string) => path.startsWith("staff/");
const insideModeration = (path: string) => path.startsWith("moderation/");

function findViolations(files: SourceFile[], publicNames: Set<string>, authNames: Set<string>): string[] {
  const violations: string[] = [];
  for (const { path, source } of files) {
    for (const spec of specifiers(source)) {
      if (!spec.startsWith(".")) continue;
      const target = posix.normalize(posix.join(posix.dirname(path), spec)).replace(/\.ts$/, "");
      for (const module of MODULES) {
        if (path.startsWith(`${module}/`)) continue;
        if (target.startsWith(`${module}/`) && target !== `${module}/index`) {
          violations.push(`${path}: imports ${spec}, which is inside the ${module} module (use ./${module})`);
        }
      }
    }
    if (!insideAuth(path) && !AUTH_POOL_ALLOWED.has(path) && /\b(DATABASE_URL_AUTH|authDb)\b/.test(source)) {
      violations.push(`${path}: references the auth database pool`);
    }
    // Each encryption key with the list of the keys it replaced: after a rotation those still open what was stored before it.
    if (!insideAuth(path) && !AUTH_KEYS_ALLOWED.has(path) && /\b(TOTP_ENC_KEY|TOTP_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS|NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY|NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS|AUTH_HMAC_KEY|IP_HASH_KEY)\b/.test(source)) {
      violations.push(`${path}: references an auth key`);
    }
    if (insideAuth(path)) {
      for (const name of dbImports(source)) {
        if (name === "*") violations.push(`${path}: namespace import of @korbat/db (import auth-schema names explicitly)`);
        else if (publicNames.has(name)) violations.push(`${path}: imports public-schema ${name} from @korbat/db`);
      }
    }
    if (!insideMedia(path) && /\b(postMedia|post_media)\b/.test(source)) {
      violations.push(`${path}: references post_media, which only the media module may touch`);
    }
    // The staff module (role korbat_api) reads and writes the public audit log; staff keys, staff sessions and enrolments
    // are credentials, the auth module's alone (3a design, section 5). The moderation module owns the moderation tables on
    // the same role: a notifier's contact and the staff links live in the auth schema, out of its reach (3c design, section 5).
    if (insideSocial(path) || insideMedia(path) || insideStaff(path) || insideModeration(path)) {
      for (const name of dbImports(source)) {
        if (name === "*") violations.push(`${path}: namespace import of @korbat/db (import public-schema names explicitly)`);
        else if (authNames.has(name)) violations.push(`${path}: imports auth-schema ${name} from @korbat/db`);
      }
    }
    // The account module sequences the other three through their index files and holds no table access of its own
    // (1b spec, section 5): no table or enum of either schema may be named in it. Db and DbTx, which are not schema
    // names, stay allowed, since a transaction is passed through it.
    if (insideAccount(path)) {
      for (const name of dbImports(source)) {
        if (name === "*") violations.push(`${path}: namespace import of @korbat/db (the account module holds no table access)`);
        else if (publicNames.has(name)) violations.push(`${path}: imports public-schema ${name} from @korbat/db (the account module holds no table access)`);
        else if (authNames.has(name)) violations.push(`${path}: imports auth-schema ${name} from @korbat/db (the account module holds no table access)`);
      }
    }
    // The staff module uses the auth module's interface as the other modules do, never its repository or its session
    // store, which would hand it the auth tables; the moderation module likewise. Any mention counts, so a renamed,
    // namespace or dynamic import is caught as surely as a named one.
    if (insideStaff(path) || insideModeration(path)) {
      const module = insideStaff(path) ? "staff" : "moderation";
      for (const name of new Set([...source.matchAll(/\b(createAuthRepo|createSessions)\b/g)].map((m) => m[1]!))) {
        violations.push(`${path}: uses the auth module's ${name} (the ${module} module goes through the auth module's interface)`);
      }
    }
  }
  return violations;
}

/**
 * The source pins of the freeze (3c design, sections 6.1 and 6.5). The freeze of the path for suspected child sexual abuse
 * material holds only while every path of a kind passes one gate, so who may name what is pinned here, beside the
 * database's own pins of who names the predicate there:
 *   - `post_frozen` is named only in the media repository and the moderation repository, and `frozen_for` nowhere in the
 *     API: no other file decides by itself what is frozen;
 *   - a delete of `post_media` is written only in the media repository, whose every delete the keep trigger judges and
 *     whose every answer names only rows that are gone;
 *   - `requestDeletion` (asking the worker to delete an image's files) and `openImage` (opening an image file of the
 *     store) are named in a pinned list of files, each a pinned number of times, comments included: a new caller of
 *     either fails the test until whoever adds it has checked it against the gates and listed it.
 */
const POST_FROZEN_ALLOWED = new Set(["media/repo.ts", "moderation/repo.ts"]);
const POST_MEDIA_DELETE_ALLOWED = new Set(["media/repo.ts"]);
const POST_MEDIA_DELETE = /\bdelete\s+from\s+(?:only\s+)?(?:"?public"?\s*\.\s*)?"?post_media\b|\btruncate\b[^;`]*\bpost_media\b|\.delete\(\s*postMedia\b/i;

function findFreezeViolations(files: SourceFile[]): string[] {
  const violations: string[] = [];
  for (const { path, source } of files) {
    if (/\bfrozen_for\b/.test(source)) violations.push(`${path}: names frozen_for, which only the database's own functions name`);
    if (/\bpost_frozen\b/.test(source) && !POST_FROZEN_ALLOWED.has(path)) violations.push(`${path}: names post_frozen, which only the media and moderation repositories may`);
    if (POST_MEDIA_DELETE.test(source) && !POST_MEDIA_DELETE_ALLOWED.has(path)) violations.push(`${path}: deletes from post_media, which only the media repository may`);
  }
  return violations;
}

/** Every file that names `name` as a whole word, with how often, comments included. */
function mentions(files: SourceFile[], name: string): Record<string, number> {
  const found: Record<string, number> = {};
  for (const { path, source } of files) {
    // Cut at every word boundary: a whole word is then a piece of its own.
    const count = source.split(/\b/).filter((piece) => piece === name).length;
    if (count > 0) found[path] = count;
  }
  return found;
}

/**
 * Where `requestDeletion` is named. A deletion request names an id that a delete of post_media answered, an upload that
 * failed before it could be put on a post, or a file that has no row: the files module writes the request; the upload's
 * removal, the sweeper, the author's deletion (after its commit), the account's purge (after its commit) and the
 * disposal's caller (after its commit) ask for it through the module's interfaces; and the one retry of what the purge
 * and the disposal owe asks for it only for a row that is gone.
 */
const REQUEST_DELETION = {
  "account/flows/deletion.ts": 1,
  "media/cases.ts": 4,
  "media/context.ts": 2,
  "media/files.ts": 1,
  "media/flows/remove.ts": 1,
  "media/index.ts": 5,
  // The retry of owed deletions, which asks only for ids whose row it found gone.
  "media/owed.ts": 1,
  "media/sweeper.ts": 2,
  // The retention job, which asks for a batch's files after the commit of the transaction that deleted their rows.
  "moderation/retention.ts": 1,
  "social/context.ts": 1,
  "social/flows/posts.ts": 1,
};

/**
 * Where `openImage` is named: the files module, which opens a file of the store under its checks, and its three callers,
 * each behind its own reader's rule: serve (gate S), the export's open (which reads the row again) and the staff's image
 * (gate V).
 */
const OPEN_IMAGE = {
  "media/cases.ts": 1,
  "media/files.ts": 1,
  "media/flows/serve.ts": 1,
  "media/index.ts": 1,
};

describe("the freeze's source pins", () => {
  test("apps/api/src names post_frozen only in the two repositories, frozen_for nowhere, and deletes from post_media only in the media repository", () => {
    expect(findFreezeViolations(loadSources())).toEqual([]);
    // The media repository does name the predicate and does delete: the pins are about a file that exists.
    const repo = loadSources().find((file) => file.path === "media/repo.ts")!;
    expect(repo.source).toMatch(/\bpost_frozen\b/);
    expect(POST_MEDIA_DELETE.test(repo.source)).toBe(true);
  });

  test("catches the predicate named outside the two repositories, and its core named anywhere", () => {
    const files: SourceFile[] = [
      { path: "media/repo.ts", source: "sql`select public.post_frozen(m.post_id) as frozen from post_media m`" },
      { path: "moderation/repo.ts", source: "sql`select not public.post_frozen(${postId}::uuid) as images_allowed`" },
      { path: "moderation/cases.ts", source: "const [row] = await tx.execute(sql`select public.post_frozen(${postId}::uuid) as frozen`);" },
      { path: "media/flows/serve.ts", source: "const frozen = await db.execute(sql`select post_frozen(${postId})`);" },
      { path: "staff/cases.ts", source: "await db.execute(sql`select public.frozen_for(${postId}::uuid, ${authorId}::uuid)`);" },
      { path: "media/repo.ts", source: "sql`select public.frozen_for(m.post_id, m.owner_id) from post_media m`" },
      // Another word that only contains the name is not the name.
      { path: "social/views.ts", source: "const post_frozen_label = 1; const unfrozen_for_now = 2;" },
    ];
    expect(findFreezeViolations(files)).toEqual([
      "moderation/cases.ts: names post_frozen, which only the media and moderation repositories may",
      "media/flows/serve.ts: names post_frozen, which only the media and moderation repositories may",
      "staff/cases.ts: names frozen_for, which only the database's own functions name",
      "media/repo.ts: names frozen_for, which only the database's own functions name",
    ]);
  });

  test("catches a delete of post_media outside the media repository, in SQL and through the query builder", () => {
    const files: SourceFile[] = [
      { path: "media/repo.ts", source: "await tx.execute(sql`delete from post_media where id in (select id from post_media where post_id = ${postId}::uuid order by id for update) returning id`);\nawait db.delete(postMedia).where(eq(postMedia.id, id));" },
      { path: "media/sweeper.ts", source: "await db.execute(sql`delete from post_media where post_id is null and created_at < ${before}`);" },
      { path: "media/flows/remove.ts", source: "await deps.db.delete(postMedia).where(eq(postMedia.id, id));" },
      { path: "media/cases.ts", source: 'await tx.execute(sql`DELETE FROM "public"."post_media" WHERE "id" = ${id}`);' },
      { path: "media/index.ts", source: "await tx.execute(sql`truncate table post_media cascade`);" },
      // Reading and updating image rows, and deleting something else, is not a delete of image rows.
      { path: "media/flows/status.ts", source: "await db.update(postMedia).set({ status }).where(eq(postMedia.id, id));\nawait db.delete(posts).where(eq(posts.id, id));\nconst rows = await db.execute(sql`select id from post_media`);" },
    ];
    expect(findFreezeViolations(files)).toEqual([
      "media/sweeper.ts: deletes from post_media, which only the media repository may",
      "media/flows/remove.ts: deletes from post_media, which only the media repository may",
      "media/cases.ts: deletes from post_media, which only the media repository may",
      "media/index.ts: deletes from post_media, which only the media repository may",
    ]);
  });

  test("requestDeletion and openImage are named in exactly the pinned files, each the pinned number of times", () => {
    expect(mentions(loadSources(), "requestDeletion")).toEqual(REQUEST_DELETION);
    expect(mentions(loadSources(), "openImage")).toEqual(OPEN_IMAGE);
  });

  test("catches a new caller of either, in a file of the list and in one outside it", () => {
    const real = loadSources();
    // A second request in the purge's flow, and a first one in a file that had none.
    const withCallers = real
      .map((file) => (file.path === "account/flows/deletion.ts" ? { ...file, source: `${file.source}\nawait deps.media.requestDeletion(kept);` } : file))
      .concat([{ path: "moderation/decide.ts", source: "await deps.media.requestDeletion(ids);" }]);
    expect(mentions(withCallers, "requestDeletion")).not.toEqual(REQUEST_DELETION);
    expect(mentions(withCallers, "requestDeletion")).toMatchObject({ "account/flows/deletion.ts": 2, "moderation/decide.ts": 1 });
    // A fourth opener of the store's files.
    const withOpener = real.concat([{ path: "staff/cases.ts", source: 'const file = await files.openImage(id, "large");' }]);
    expect(mentions(withOpener, "openImage")).not.toEqual(OPEN_IMAGE);
    // A name that only contains the word is not counted.
    expect(mentions([{ path: "x.ts", source: "requestDeletions(); reopenImage(); openImages();" }], "requestDeletion")).toEqual({});
    expect(mentions([{ path: "x.ts", source: "requestDeletions(); reopenImage(); openImages();" }], "openImage")).toEqual({});
  });
});

/**
 * The source pins of account sanctions (3e design, sections 11 and 12.2; invariant 23): no write of an account is added
 * without the one predicate.
 *   - The predicate's three fragments, exported by lib/standing.ts (`liveNotSuspended`, and the two halves that a locking
 *     statement answers separately, `suspendedAt` and `reportsRestrictedAt`), are named in a pinned list of files, each a
 *     pinned number of times, comments included, as REQUEST_DELETION is: whoever adds a write on behalf of an account adds
 *     its site to the list, and the auth module never names one. So is the closing judgment (`closingJudgment`, 3e's
 *     review), the last statement of a write's transaction, which reads both halves.
 *   - The profile's three derived columns are named in apps/api/src only in lib/standing.ts, social/repo.ts's
 *     lockAccounts and the moderation module's standing-repo.ts, in SQL or by drizzle's names: no other file decides by
 *     itself whether an account is suspended. Their one writer is the database's standing_apply (the function pin of 6.6).
 */
const STANDING_PREDICATE = {
  // social/repo.ts, 3e Task 6: Explore's round applies the predicate to the candidates' authors and to the engagers at the
  // round's time, and the page and the chip to the authors at the read's (explorePage, listedInExplore).
  liveNotSuspended: { "lib/standing.ts": 1, "media/repo.ts": 2, "profiles/store.ts": 3, "social/repo.ts": 6 },
  // social/repo.ts, 3e Task 6: the author's Explore status reads whether the author is suspended (exploreFacts). lib/standing.ts,
  // 3e's review: the closing judgment reads both halves.
  suspendedAt: { "lib/standing.ts": 3, "social/repo.ts": 7 },
  reportsRestrictedAt: { "lib/standing.ts": 2, "social/repo.ts": 2 },
  // 3e's review (database1): the writes that end with the closing judgment: the social repository's (judgeActing), the
  // upload's row, and the intake of a report under a rule. The profile store's badge and the profile's edit end with
  // their UPDATE, made once the row is held.
  closingJudgment: { "lib/standing.ts": 1, "media/repo.ts": 2, "moderation/intake.ts": 2, "social/repo.ts": 2 },
};
const STANDING_COLUMNS_ALLOWED = new Set(["lib/standing.ts", "social/repo.ts", "moderation/standing-repo.ts"]);
const STANDING_COLUMNS = ["suspended_from", "suspended_until", "reports_restricted_until", "suspendedFrom", "suspendedUntil", "reportsRestrictedUntil"];
/** Whether a file names one of the derived columns as a whole word, by the same cut as `mentions`. */
const namesStandingColumn = (file: SourceFile): boolean => STANDING_COLUMNS.some((name) => mentions([file], name)[file.path] !== undefined);

function findStandingViolations(files: SourceFile[]): string[] {
  return files.filter((file) => namesStandingColumn(file) && !STANDING_COLUMNS_ALLOWED.has(file.path)).map(({ path }) => `${path}: names a derived column of an account's standing, which only lib/standing.ts, social/repo.ts and moderation/standing-repo.ts may`);
}

describe("the source pins of account sanctions (3e)", () => {
  test("the predicate's fragments are named in exactly the pinned files, each the pinned number of times; the auth module names none", () => {
    for (const [name, pinned] of Object.entries(STANDING_PREDICATE)) expect(mentions(loadSources(), name), name).toEqual(pinned);
    // The auth module names none: no file of it is in any of the pinned lists.
    for (const pinned of Object.values(STANDING_PREDICATE)) expect(Object.keys(pinned).filter((path) => path.startsWith("auth/"))).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("catches a new write that names the predicate, in a pinned file and in one outside the list", () => {
    const real = loadSources();
    const withWrites = real
      .map((file) => (file.path === "media/repo.ts" ? { ...file, source: file.source + String.fromCharCode(10) + 'sql`update post_media set alt = null where ${liveNotSuspended("p", WRITE_CLOCK)}`;' } : file))
      .concat([{ path: "moderation/texts.ts", source: 'await tx.execute(sql`select 1 from profiles p where ${suspendedAt("p", WRITE_CLOCK)}`);' }]);
    expect(mentions(withWrites, "liveNotSuspended")).not.toEqual(STANDING_PREDICATE.liveNotSuspended);
    expect(mentions(withWrites, "liveNotSuspended")).toMatchObject({ "media/repo.ts": 3 });
    expect(mentions(withWrites, "suspendedAt")).toMatchObject({ "moderation/texts.ts": 1 });
    expect(mentions(withWrites, "suspendedAt")).not.toEqual(STANDING_PREDICATE.suspendedAt);
  });

  test("the three derived columns are named only in lib/standing.ts, social/repo.ts and moderation/standing-repo.ts, and lib/standing.ts does name them", () => {
    expect(findStandingViolations(loadSources())).toEqual([]);
    expect(namesStandingColumn(loadSources().find((file) => file.path === "lib/standing.ts")!)).toBe(true);
  });

  test("catches a derived column named elsewhere, in SQL and by drizzle's name", () => {
    const files: SourceFile[] = [
      { path: "lib/standing.ts", source: "sql`(${p}.suspended_from is not null and ${p}.suspended_from <= ${at} and ${at} < ${p}.suspended_until)`" },
      { path: "moderation/standing-repo.ts", source: "sql`select reports_restricted_until from profiles`" },
      { path: "social/flows/posts.ts", source: "const [row] = await db.execute(sql`select suspended_until from profiles where id = ${viewer}::uuid`);" },
      { path: "media/repo.ts", source: "await db.select({ until: profiles.suspendedUntil }).from(profiles);" },
      { path: "auth/flows/badge.ts", source: "if (profile.reportsRestrictedUntil) return;" },
      // A word that only contains the name is not the name.
      { path: "social/views.ts", source: "const unsuspended_from_now = 1;" },
    ];
    expect(findStandingViolations(files)).toEqual([
      "social/flows/posts.ts: names a derived column of an account's standing, which only lib/standing.ts, social/repo.ts and moderation/standing-repo.ts may",
      "media/repo.ts: names a derived column of an account's standing, which only lib/standing.ts, social/repo.ts and moderation/standing-repo.ts may",
      "auth/flows/badge.ts: names a derived column of an account's standing, which only lib/standing.ts, social/repo.ts and moderation/standing-repo.ts may",
    ]);
  });
});

/**
 * The watcher's boundary (3f design, section 5): notify, an entry point of its own (dist/notify.js), imports the contracts,
 * the database package and Node's and its packages' modules, and nothing of the API's: no relative import leaves
 * src/notify. Nothing outside it imports it either: the API holds no mailbox credential, no ntfy token and no route to the
 * push network, and the watcher shares no code with the API that could carry one in.
 */
function findNotifyViolations(files: SourceFile[]): string[] {
  const violations: string[] = [];
  for (const { path, source } of files) {
    const inside = path.startsWith("notify/");
    for (const spec of specifiers(source)) {
      if (!spec.startsWith(".")) continue;
      const target = posix.normalize(posix.join(posix.dirname(path), spec));
      if (inside && !target.startsWith("notify/")) violations.push(`${path}: imports ${spec}, outside the watcher`);
      if (!inside && target.startsWith("notify/")) violations.push(`${path}: imports ${spec}, inside the watcher`);
    }
  }
  return violations;
}

describe("the watcher's boundary (3f)", () => {
  test("src/notify imports nothing of the API's modules, and nothing imports src/notify", () => {
    const files = loadSources();
    expect(files.filter((file) => file.path.startsWith("notify/")).map((file) => file.path).sort()).toEqual(["notify/imap.ts", "notify/main.ts", "notify/push.ts"]);
    expect(findNotifyViolations(files)).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("catches an import of an API module from the watcher, and an import of the watcher from the API", () => {
    expect(
      findNotifyViolations([
        { path: "notify/main.ts", source: 'import { loadConfig } from "../config"; import { publish } from "./push";' },
        { path: "notify/push.ts", source: 'import { staffAlert } from "../moderation";' },
        { path: "moderation/alerts.ts", source: 'import { TOPICS } from "../notify/push";' },
        { path: "index.ts", source: 'import { ALERT_KINDS } from "@korbat/contracts";' },
      ]),
    ).toEqual(["notify/main.ts: imports ../config, outside the watcher", "notify/push.ts: imports ../moderation, outside the watcher", "moderation/alerts.ts: imports ../notify/push, inside the watcher"]);
  });
});

/**
 * The hand-over's boundary (3f design, section 5 and invariant 16): handover.ts, an entry point of its own
 * (dist/handover.js), imports nothing under ./ (no module of the API, so no database, no configuration and no copy of
 * anything that could reach either) and only Node's own modules, none of which opens a socket or a process; nothing
 * imports it. And no file outside media/ but config.ts and index.ts names the store's directory setting, MEDIA_STORE_DIR:
 * the store is read through the media module, or by the hand-over's program under its fixed mount.
 */
const SOCKET_MODULES = new Set(["node:net", "node:http", "node:https", "node:http2", "node:dgram", "node:tls", "node:child_process", "node:worker_threads", "node:cluster"]);
function findHandoverViolations(files: SourceFile[]): string[] {
  const violations: string[] = [];
  for (const { path, source } of files) {
    for (const spec of specifiers(source)) {
      if (path === "handover.ts") {
        if (spec.startsWith(".")) violations.push(`${path}: imports ${spec}, a module of the API`);
        else if (!spec.startsWith("node:")) violations.push(`${path}: imports ${spec}, which is not one of Node's own modules`);
        else if (SOCKET_MODULES.has(spec)) violations.push(`${path}: imports ${spec}, which can open a socket or a process`);
      } else if (spec.startsWith(".") && posix.normalize(posix.join(posix.dirname(path), spec)).replace(/[.]ts$/, "") === "handover") {
        violations.push(`${path}: imports ${spec}, the hand-over's program`);
      }
    }
    if (/MEDIA_STORE_DIR/.test(source) && !path.startsWith("media/") && path !== "config.ts" && path !== "index.ts") {
      violations.push(`${path}: names MEDIA_STORE_DIR, which only the media module, config.ts and index.ts may`);
    }
  }
  return violations;
}

describe("the hand-over's boundary (3f Task 5)", () => {
  test("handover.ts imports only Node's own modules and none that opens a socket, nothing imports it, and no file outside media/ but config.ts and index.ts names the store's directory setting", () => {
    const files = loadSources();
    expect(files.map((file) => file.path)).toContain("handover.ts");
    expect(findHandoverViolations(files)).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("catches an import of an API module or a package from the hand-over, a socket's module, an import of the hand-over, and the store's setting named elsewhere", () => {
    expect(
      findHandoverViolations([
        { path: "handover.ts", source: 'import { storedImageName } from "./media"; import { sql } from "drizzle-orm"; import { connect } from "node:net"; import { crc32 } from "node:zlib";' },
        { path: "cli/records.ts", source: 'import { zipStored } from "../handover";' },
        { path: "cli/staff.ts", source: "const dir = env.MEDIA_STORE_DIR;" },
        { path: "media/files.ts", source: "const dir = config.MEDIA_STORE_DIR;" },
      ]),
    ).toEqual([
      "handover.ts: imports ./media, a module of the API",
      "handover.ts: imports drizzle-orm, which is not one of Node's own modules",
      "handover.ts: imports node:net, which can open a socket or a process",
      "cli/records.ts: imports ../handover, the hand-over's program",
      "cli/staff.ts: names MEDIA_STORE_DIR, which only the media module, config.ts and index.ts may",
    ]);
  });
});

/**
 * The quarantine's mover (3d design, section 5 "The services"; 12.1 rows 13 and 14): quarantine.ts, an entry point of its
 * own (dist/quarantine.js), is as bare as the hand-over: it imports nothing under ./ and only Node's own modules, none
 * that opens a socket or a process, and nothing imports it.
 */
function findQuarantineViolations(files: SourceFile[]): string[] {
  const violations: string[] = [];
  for (const { path, source } of files) {
    for (const spec of specifiers(source)) {
      if (path === "quarantine.ts") {
        if (spec.startsWith(".")) violations.push(`${path}: imports ${spec}, a module of the API`);
        else if (!spec.startsWith("node:")) violations.push(`${path}: imports ${spec}, which is not one of Node's own modules`);
        else if (SOCKET_MODULES.has(spec)) violations.push(`${path}: imports ${spec}, which can open a socket or a process`);
      } else if (spec.startsWith(".") && posix.normalize(posix.join(posix.dirname(path), spec)).replace(/[.]ts$/, "") === "quarantine") {
        violations.push(`${path}: imports ${spec}, the quarantine's mover`);
      }
    }
  }
  return violations;
}

const REPO_ROOT = fileURLToPath(new URL("../../../", import.meta.url));
const LF = String.fromCharCode(10);

/** The service blocks of a Compose file's services section, by name, as text: from a service's name to the next one's. */
function composeServices(text: string): Map<string, string> {
  const head = `${LF}services:${LF}`;
  const section = text.slice(text.indexOf(head) + head.length - 1);
  // The section ends at the next top-level key.
  const end = section.slice(1).search(new RegExp(`${LF}[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*:`));
  const body = end === -1 ? section : section.slice(0, end + 1);
  const blocks = new Map<string, string>();
  const names = [...body.matchAll(new RegExp(`${LF} {2}([a-z][a-z0-9_-]*):${LF}`, "g"))];
  names.forEach((match, i) => blocks.set(match[1]!, body.slice(match.index!, names[i + 1]?.index ?? body.length)));
  return blocks;
}

/**
 * Who mounts the quarantine (3d design, section 5; 12.1 row 14): in compose.yml only `quarantine`, read-write, and
 * `handover`, read-only, name the volume media-quarantine, and compose.dev.yml names it nowhere, so neither the api, the
 * migrate nor the worker service mounts it. The mover has no network, no environment, every capability dropped, a
 * read-only root and the two volumes alone; the worker keeps network_mode: none.
 */
function findComposeViolations(compose: string, dev: string): string[] {
  const violations: string[] = [];
  const services = composeServices(compose);
  for (const [name, block] of services) {
    const mounts = block.split(LF).filter((line) => line.includes("media-quarantine"));
    if (mounts.length === 0) continue;
    const expected = name === "quarantine" ? "- media-quarantine:/media/quarantine" : name === "handover" ? "- media-quarantine:/media/quarantine:ro" : null;
    if (expected === null) violations.push(`compose.yml: ${name} names media-quarantine`);
    else if (mounts.map((line) => line.trim()).join("|") !== expected) violations.push(`compose.yml: ${name} mounts media-quarantine otherwise than ${expected}`);
  }
  for (const [name, block] of composeServices(dev)) {
    if (block.includes("media-quarantine")) violations.push(`compose.dev.yml: ${name} names media-quarantine`);
  }
  const mover = services.get("quarantine");
  if (!mover) violations.push("compose.yml: no service quarantine");
  else {
    for (const line of ["network_mode: none", "read_only: true", "cap_drop: [ALL]", '"no-new-privileges:true"', 'profiles: ["quarantine"]', 'entrypoint: ["node", "dist/quarantine.js", "/media/store", "/media/quarantine"]']) {
      if (!mover.includes(line)) violations.push(`compose.yml: quarantine lacks ${line}`);
    }
    for (const key of ["environment:", "env_file:", "networks:", "ports:", "secrets:"]) {
      if (mover.includes(key)) violations.push(`compose.yml: quarantine has ${key}`);
    }
    const volumes = mover
      .split(LF)
      .filter((line) => /^ {6}- /.test(line))
      .map((line) => line.trim());
    if (volumes.join("|") !== "- media-store:/media/store|- media-quarantine:/media/quarantine") violations.push(`compose.yml: quarantine mounts ${volumes.join(", ")}`);
  }
  if (!services.get("worker")?.includes("network_mode: none")) violations.push("compose.yml: worker has a network");
  return violations;
}

describe("the quarantine's boundary (3d Task 1)", () => {
  test("quarantine.ts imports only Node's own modules and none that opens a socket, and nothing imports it", () => {
    const files = loadSources();
    expect(files.map((file) => file.path)).toContain("quarantine.ts");
    expect(findQuarantineViolations(files)).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("catches an import of an API module or a package from the mover, a socket's module, and an import of the mover", () => {
    expect(
      findQuarantineViolations([
        { path: "quarantine.ts", source: 'import { storedImageName } from "./media"; import { z } from "zod"; import { request } from "node:https"; import { open } from "node:fs/promises";' },
        { path: "cli/custody.ts", source: 'import { runQuarantine } from "../quarantine";' },
      ]),
    ).toEqual([
      "quarantine.ts: imports ./media, a module of the API",
      "quarantine.ts: imports zod, which is not one of Node's own modules",
      "quarantine.ts: imports node:https, which can open a socket or a process",
      "cli/custody.ts: imports ../quarantine, the quarantine's mover",
    ]);
  });

  test("only quarantine (read-write) and handover (read-only) mount media-quarantine; the mover is bare and the worker keeps no network", () => {
    const compose = readFileSync(join(REPO_ROOT, "infra", "compose.yml"), "utf8");
    const dev = readFileSync(join(REPO_ROOT, "infra", "compose.dev.yml"), "utf8");
    expect([...composeServices(compose).keys()]).toEqual(expect.arrayContaining(["api", "migrate", "worker", "handover", "quarantine"]));
    expect(findComposeViolations(compose, dev)).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("catches the volume in the api or the development file, a writable hand-over and a mover with an environment", () => {
    const compose = readFileSync(join(REPO_ROOT, "infra", "compose.yml"), "utf8");
    const dev = readFileSync(join(REPO_ROOT, "infra", "compose.dev.yml"), "utf8");
    const broken = compose
      .replace(`      - media-store:/media/store:ro${LF}      - media-quarantine:/media/quarantine:ro`, `      - media-store:/media/store:ro${LF}      - media-quarantine:/media/quarantine`)
      .replace(`      - media-uploads:/media/uploads${LF}`, `      - media-uploads:/media/uploads${LF}      - media-quarantine:/media/quarantine:ro${LF}`)
      .replace(`    profiles: ["quarantine"]${LF}`, `    profiles: ["quarantine"]${LF}    environment:${LF}      X: "1"${LF}`);
    const devBroken = dev.replace(`  api:${LF}`, `  api:${LF}    volumes: [media-quarantine:/media/quarantine]${LF}`);
    expect(findComposeViolations(broken, devBroken)).toEqual([
      "compose.yml: api names media-quarantine",
      "compose.yml: handover mounts media-quarantine otherwise than - media-quarantine:/media/quarantine:ro",
      "compose.dev.yml: api names media-quarantine",
      "compose.yml: quarantine has environment:",
    ]);
  });
});

/**
 * The adapters' files (3d design, section 5 "The adapters"): each adapter is a file of its own that imports nothing of its
 * module, so it is given what its interface names and nothing more: no media file, no repository and no database. Task
 * 3 builds the first, the edge's purge (media/edge-adapter.ts); the matcher's (media/match-adapter.ts) and the witness's
 * (transparency/witness.ts) join this list with the tasks that build them. A package import that is no database stays
 * allowed: the adapter reads its numbers from the contracts.
 */
const ADAPTER_FILES = ["media/edge-adapter.ts"];
function findAdapterViolations(files: SourceFile[]): string[] {
  const violations: string[] = [];
  for (const { path, source } of files) {
    if (!ADAPTER_FILES.includes(path)) continue;
    for (const spec of specifiers(source)) {
      if (spec.startsWith(".")) violations.push(`${path}: imports ${spec}, a file of the API`);
      else if (spec.startsWith("@korbat/db")) violations.push(`${path}: imports ${spec}, the database`);
    }
  }
  return violations;
}

describe("the adapters' files (3d Task 3)", () => {
  test("each adapter's file exists and imports nothing of its module, no repository and no database", () => {
    const files = loadSources();
    for (const path of ADAPTER_FILES) expect(files.map((file) => file.path), path).toContain(path);
    expect(findAdapterViolations(files)).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("catches an adapter that imports the media repository, a module's file, its index or the database", () => {
    expect(
      findAdapterViolations([
        { path: "media/edge-adapter.ts", source: 'import { createMediaRepo } from "./repo"; import type { MediaDeps } from "./context"; import { postMedia } from "@korbat/db"; import { EDGE_RULES } from "@korbat/contracts";' },
        { path: "media/edge.ts", source: 'import { createMediaRepo } from "./repo";' },
      ]),
    ).toEqual(["media/edge-adapter.ts: imports ./repo, a file of the API", "media/edge-adapter.ts: imports ./context, a file of the API", "media/edge-adapter.ts: imports @korbat/db, the database"]);
    expect(findAdapterViolations([{ path: "media/edge-adapter.ts", source: 'import { media } from "../media";' }])).toEqual(["media/edge-adapter.ts: imports ../media, a file of the API"]);
  });
});

describe("module boundaries", () => {
  test("walks the real source tree", () => {
    const paths = loadSources().map((f) => f.path);
    expect(paths).toContain("auth/index.ts");
    expect(paths).toContain("social/index.ts");
    expect(paths).toContain("media/index.ts");
    expect(paths).toContain("account/index.ts");
    expect(paths).toContain("staff/index.ts");
    expect(paths).toContain("moderation/index.ts");
    expect(paths).toContain("cli/staff.ts");
    expect(paths).toContain("app.ts");
    expect(publicSchemaNames()).toContain("profiles");
    expect(publicSchemaNames()).not.toContain("users");
    expect(authSchemaNames()).toContain("users");
    expect(authSchemaNames()).not.toContain("posts");
  });

  test("apps/api/src has no boundary violations", () => {
```
