- `API_SMTP_URL` and `API_MAIL_FROM` to the EU mail relay; a plain `smtp://` relay must offer STARTTLS, which the API requires in production.
- `API_WEBAUTHN_RP_ID` before the first passkey is registered, when it should differ from the host of `API_APP_ORIGIN`; changing it afterwards strands every passkey. The staff console does not use it: staff keys are bound to the console's own relying party ID.
- `API_CONSOLE_ORIGIN` to the staff console's public origin, for example `https://korbat-staff.example`, preferably on a registrable domain of its own so browsers treat the app and the console as different sites (a subdomain of the app's domain works too), and `API_CONSOLE_RP_ID` left empty, so staff keys are bound to that hostname. Production refuses a plain-http console, an IP address or `localhost`, the app's hostname on any port, a console on a parent domain of the app's hostname, and a relying party ID other than the console's hostname or equal to the app's; no environment accepts the console's origin in `API_TRUSTED_ORIGINS`. Empty, the console is off. From sub-project 3c only the console decides reports and notices; with it off they are taken and wait, and staff are alerted to them.
- `WEB_CONTACT_EMAIL` to the users' contact address, which the report form names when the human check fails or the limits are reached and which the terms page shows; the web image refuses to build without one, and a production build refuses a placeholder (a domain ending in `.local`, `.localhost`, `.test`, `.invalid` or `.example`, or `example.com`, `example.org` or `example.net`). Its mailbox is set to load no remote content, and to keep deleted mail no longer than its host's shortest setting; a person reads it every working day (Moderation, the runbook's bullet on the users' contact mailbox). Since sub-project 3f the authorities' contact address is published as well, as `API_CONTACT_POINT` for the API and `WEB_CONTACT_POINT` for the web build, with korbat's state as `API_HOME_STATE` and `WEB_HOME_STATE`, the last step of the owner's list below: with the languages it may be addressed in, among them an official language of korbat's home state (DSA Art. 11(3), TCO Art. 15(2)), and notified to the national authorities where the home state requires it.
- `API_MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR` to the hour of the UTC day, 0 to 23, at which the day's decisions on reports and notices are released to those who sent them, in one batch, so that nobody can tell from a mail's minute when a decision was made; empty means 7.
- `API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY` generated (`node scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs` fills a placeholder), backed up off the server and rotated as the paragraph below says; `API_MODERATION_DEFER_UNPROVEN=off` and `API_MODERATION_RETENTION=on`, their defaults (Moderation says when each is changed).
- `KORBAT_ENV=production` before building the images; it is the API's `NODE_ENV` too, so the guards above are on.
- `TUNNEL=on` and `API_TRUST_PROXY=cloudflare` when cloudflared is the only way in (the app's public hostname points at `http://caddy:8080`, and the console's at `http://caddy:8090`, below); `TUNNEL=off` and `API_TRUST_PROXY=caddy` when Caddy's port is reachable directly. With `on`, Caddy keeps `CF-Connecting-IP` for the API; with `off` it drops it, so nobody can claim an address.
- In Cloudflare, set Browser Cache TTL to "Respect Existing Headers", or browsers keep images for four hours whatever the server says.

Keep `API_AUTH_HMAC_KEY`, `API_IP_HASH_KEY`, `API_TOTP_ENC_KEY` and `API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY` secret and backed up. Losing `API_TOTP_ENC_KEY` breaks every enrolled authenticator. To rotate it, put the old key in `API_TOTP_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS` and a new `v2:` key in `API_TOTP_ENC_KEY`; each secret is re-encrypted with the new key when it is next used. Without `API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY` korbat can neither mail a signed-out notifier nor say who sent a notice. To rotate `API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY`, put the old key in `API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS` and a new `v2:` key in `API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY`. Contacts are never re-encrypted, so the old key stays listed until no contact made under it remains, that is until `select count(*) from auth.notifier_contacts where name_enc like 'v1:%' or email_enc like 'v1:%'` answers 0. A contact can outlive 13 months while its notice is still owed a decision or a mail. Keep the old key off the server for as long as any backup holds such a contact.

Before the first report can concern a threat to someone's life or safety, obtain and record the channels for a notification under DSA Art. 18: the national police's, and Europol's for when the Member State concerned cannot be identified, each asked for beforehand from the national police or the Digital Services Coordinator (Moderation, the runbook's bullet on Art. 18).

A post that a decision withholds or removes leaves Explore at the next read, as it leaves every list; nothing acts on Explore alone. Since formula version 2 (account sanctions) a post that a later decision restores gets back the hours it was hidden, and a suspended account's posts and approvals leave the round while the suspension runs. Explore's cold start lasts about two days: only accounts at least 48 hours old count, so on a new instance Explore stays empty until the first accounts are that old.

The staff console's final hostname is chosen before the first enrolment. Staff keys are bound to it, since `API_CONSOLE_RP_ID` equals it, so moving the console later strands every staff key and means a new enrolment for every person; this includes a move to a domain of its own or behind a gate at another hostname. The tunnel gets a second public hostname, the console's, pointing at `http://caddy:8090`, with its HTTP Host Header setting left empty, so the API sees the console's hostname. Cloudflare Access in front keeps the hostname and the keys. A WireGuard or Tailscale gate keeps them only if it serves the same hostname over https with a certificate of its own, because Caddy runs with `auto_https off` while TLS ends at Cloudflare. Rocket Loader, Zaraz and Web Analytics stay off for the console's hostname, through a configuration rule for that hostname: the console's policy would block every script they add. Each staff member enrols two keys.

Who can rewrite the audit log: the PostgreSQL superuser, the owner `korbat_migrate` (its password is in `infra/.env`, and the migrate service uses it at every start), and anyone with Docker access on the host (psql inside the postgres container is the superuser without a password). Any of them can change a row, recompute every later hash and move the head, and a plain `audit-verify` then passes; only a place kept before the change, by someone other than the person who made it, shows the change. Until sub-project 3d publishes the head, that is the kept-head practice of the runbook under Staff console: each day the keeper, the staff member who does not run the server, copies the newest place and hash from the console's audit page and opens the place kept on the previous visit with "Go to place" to check its hash, and after each deploy and each week the operator runs `audit-verify` with every place the keeper has kept. In 3a the keeper's check is the only one independent of the operator, and it still reads through the operator's API, so it detects a change made in the database, not one that also changes the API's code to show the kept hashes. With one person, nothing detects the operator's own changes until 3d. Run `audit-verify` before and after every PostgreSQL major upgrade: the chain's text embeds PostgreSQL's print of the stored JSON, and a version that printed it differently would fail every row with metadata, never pass a forged one.

Counsel's list, to be answered before the gate above opens. From moderation cases: the period for which the draft of an access request's answer is kept; whether a removal of terrorist content on a notice makes korbat a provider that has taken action under TCO Art. 7(2); whether a final decision on content its author already deleted is mailed; whether, and under which national law, an access request may be restricted or deferred for a case korbat reported to an authority under DSA Art. 18 or for images it sealed for good, or that an authority's order concerns (GDPR Art. 23(1)(d)), what the answer and any extension under Art. 12(3) then say, and whether it names those authorities as recipients (Art. 15(1)(c)); whether 30 days suits the content backups hold; and every question that section 2 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-02-moderation-cases-3c-design.md` flags for counsel on the path for child sexual abuse material (its rows Suspected child sexual abuse material, Evidence, What the author sees of removed content, and Case targets and measures). From account sanctions: every question that section 2 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-09-account-sanctions-3e-design.md` flags for counsel, among them the reply window and what counts as sent, the protective suspension on images nobody assessed, termination, the restriction of reporting and its counts, how long the ledger's rows are kept, the handle retired under R4, and that korbat holds no account against its deletion. From authorities' orders: item 13 of the owner's list above, and every question that section 2 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-09-authorities-orders-3f-design.md` flags for counsel, among them what the author is told and when, the address kept while a report is owed, and the yearly report.

## Dependency audit

`pnpm audit --audit-level high` runs in CI. Two lower advisories are accepted, both in build-time tools that never see untrusted input here: `esbuild` 0.18 under drizzle-kit's config loader (its development server, which nothing starts) and `uuid` 7 under Expo's Xcode config plugin. Renovate moves them with their parents.

    keepLabel: "Keep",
    reverseLabel: "Reverse",

  /** 8.5: what each answer does, by when the reply came. */
  keep: {

    /** [replace.reply] */

  home: {
    replies: (n: number, age: string) =>
      `Replies waiting: ${n}, the oldest for ${age}. A held suspension does not start until its reply is answered, and a terminated account is not deleted before its reply is.`,
    strikes: (n: number) => `Accounts at ${STANDING_RULES.ladderStrikes} strikes: ${n}.`,
  },
  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- 3e Task 5 (design, sections 8.3, 8.4 and 8.7)
  /** 8.3: the warning about reporting and the restriction of it. Both cite R6; the composer sets it. */

    warnLabel: "Warn about reporting",
    restrictLabel: "Restrict reporting",
    /** Beside both controls. */
    rule: "Both measures cite R6; the composer sets it.",
    /** [warn.what], with the account's counts as this page read them. */
    warnWhat: (unfounded: number, reports: number) =>
      `A warning restricts nothing. It tells the account that ${unfounded} of the ${reports} reports it sent under the rules in the last ${STANDING_RULES.reportFrameDays} days were marked manifestly unfounded, lists them, and says that ${STANDING_RULES.reportRestrictMarks} marked reports among those it sends after the warning may lead to a restriction. A report counts once, however many of its items were marked, and by the day it was sent. A notice of illegal content is never counted.`,
    /** [warn.short] */
    warnShort: (unfounded: number, reports: number) =>
      `Not open: a warning needs at least ${STANDING_RULES.reportWarnMarks} marked reports among those the account sent in the last ${STANDING_RULES.reportFrameDays} days, and they must be at least half of its rule reports sent in that time. This account has ${unfounded} of ${reports}. One report never reaches the number alone.`,
    /** [warn.standing] */

"day" : "days"}, from the moment you confirm; the warning was its notice, and the restriction ends with it if the warning is lifted. At most ${STANDING_RULES.reportRestrictDays} days. Notices of illegal content, reports of child sexual abuse material and requests for re-examination stay open to it.`,
    /** [restrict.noWarning] */
    restrictNoWarning: "Not open: the account has no warning that still counts. Warn first.",
    /** [restrict.short] */
    restrictShort: (marksSince: number, warnedOn: string) => `Not open: ${marksSince} of the reports the account sent since the warning of ${warnedOn} were marked; a restriction needs ${STANDING_RULES.reportRestrictMarks}.`,
    /** [restrict.running] */
    restrictRunning: (restrictedUntil: string) => `Not open: a restriction runs until ${restrictedUntil}.`,

    daysLabel: `Days (1 to ${STANDING_RULES.reportRestrictDays})`,

    liftWarning: "Lift the warning about reporting",
    liftRestriction: "Lift the restriction of reporting",

  mark: {

    rule: `Tick only a report that anyone could see was unfounded without weighing it: it names nothing the rule could cover. The person who sent it sees the mark on their own list of reports once this answer is released to them, and can ask for a re-examination.`,
    /** [mark.never], once, when an item the decision answers cannot be marked. */

    /** [mark.undone] */

/**
 * The moderation codes the console can meet (3c design, sections 8 and 10): those of the case routes, of a decision, of
 * a review, of a finding's link and of a reveal. The codes of the app's own report form, appeal and re-examination never
 * reach the console.
 */
export const CONSOLE_MODERATION_CODES = [
  "notice_link_invalid",
  "notice_link_offsite",
  "case_changed",
  "case_closed",
  "staff_recused",
  "staff_target",
  "admin_required",
  "reviewer_conflict",
  "decision_cap",
  "profile_changed",
  "snapshot_mismatch",
  "snapshot_erased",
  "text_invalid",
  "text_quotes_user",
  "text_not_found",
  "invalid_decision",
  "image_refused",
  "reveal_refused",
  // 3e (design, section 8.9): the first three are the ones the composer meets; the other two cannot reach the console
  // today and are worded so that the table has an entry for each code of the type.
  "strike_mismatch",
  "standing_conflict",
  "ground_not_established",
  "reply_not_open",
  "reporting_restricted",
  // 3f (design, section 8.9): a message at the contact point that someone else closed meanwhile; and the refusals of
  // Task 2's order routes.
  "message_handled",
  "order_needs_message",
  "order_exists",
  "order_closed",
  "order_event_refused",
  "already_released",
  // 3f Task 3 (design, sections 8.5 and 8.9): the refusals of giving effect to an order.
  "order_changed",
  "order_not_verified",
  "order_cap",
  // 3f Task 6 (design, sections 8.7 to 8.9): a gap that is closed or that a decision does not fit, and a copy mark the
  // database did not take.
  "gap_mismatch",
  "copy_mismatch",
  // 3d Task 2 (design, section 8.8): the release's refusals and its check at commit.
  "release_not_open",
  "release_not_reported",
  "release_not_quarantined",
  "release_preserved",
  "release_no_leave",
  "release_period_unset",
  "release_period_running",
  "release_mismatch",
] as const satisfies readonly ModerationErrorCode[];
export type ConsoleModerationCode = (typeof CONSOLE_MODERATION_CODES)[number];

/** 3f Task 6 [copy.broken] (8.7): a download that broke off, whose mark the database refused or the console never sent. */
const COPY_BROKEN = "The download broke off, or its lines do not continue each other. Nothing was recorded as copied: press again.";

/** 3f [open.duplicate]: an order of this state, authority and reference is recorded already (order_exists). */
const OPEN_DUPLICATE =
  "An order of this authority with this reference is already recorded. If that record is wrong, correct it on its screen; if it is closed, an admin reopens it there. Do not open the order a second time under a changed reference.";

/** The console's words for each of them. A recusal reads the same whether the conflict concerns the author or a reporter. */

  order_cap: `You have given effect to ${ORDER_RULES.decisionsPerDay} order items in 24 hours, the most one staff account may. Another staff member goes on; tell the operator at once.`,

/** A small number as a word, as the design's sentences write it; a larger one in digits. */
const inWords = (n: number): string => ["zero", "one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight", "nine", "ten", "eleven", "twelve"][n] ?? String(n);

/** A removal order's hour (ORDER_RULES.hourMinutes) in the words the console's sentences use. */
const HOUR_WORDS = ORDER_RULES.hourMinutes === 60 ? "one hour" : `${ORDER_RULES.hourMinutes} minutes`;
/** The last choice of the form "Open an order" (Task 2), which every sentence that sends a person there names. */
const NOT_LISTED = '"The message is not listed"';

/**
 * 3f (design, sections 8.2, 8.3 and 18): the console's sentences of authorities' orders, each under the design's key
 * (`home.contact` is [home.contact]). Every number in one is printed from the answer or from ORDER_RULES, never typed, and
 * every time is the database's instant, printed by bothTimes. Later tasks of 3f add their keys here.
 */

  home: {
    title: "Authorities",
    /** [home.contact], in three parts: the words before the link to Contact point, the link's own words, and the rest. */

/**
 * 3d (design, sections 8.1, 8.2 and 8.4): the words of sealed files and their custody, the quarantine, the release and
 * held uploads, each under its key. Every number is printed from the answer or from a constant (QUARANTINE_RULES), never
 * typed; every time is the database's instant, printed by the screen with bothTimes. Task 1 has the quarantine's.
 */
export const CUSTODY_WORDS = {
  /** The home screen's block below "Authorities", each line only while it applies. */
  homeTitle: "Sealed files and programs",
  /** [home.quarantine], while a move into the quarantine or back is due. */
  homeQuarantine: (dueIn: number, dueOut: number, oldest: string) =>
    `Files to move or return: ${dueIn} images to move into the quarantine, ${dueOut} to return to the image store, the oldest due since ${oldest}. Whoever has the server runs the README's steps under Quarantine (staff.js quarantine-list). Until then a sealed image's files are still in the image store, and an image whose seal was lifted is not shown.`,
  /** Its addition once the oldest due move is older than the alert's threshold. */
  homeQuarantineLate: `More than ${QUARANTINE_RULES.dueHours} hours: every staff account is alerted daily until the move is recorded.`,
  /** [case.custody.in], on a seal for good in force. */
  custodyIn: (moved: number, files: number, movedAt: string | null) => (moved > 0 && movedAt !== null ? `Files: ${moved} of ${files} are in the quarantine, since ${movedAt}.` : "Files: not moved to the quarantine yet."),
  custodyInRest: "The others are still in the image store until whoever has the server moves them (the README, Quarantine).",
  /** [case.custody.return], while files of a lifted seal are still in the quarantine. */
  custodyReturn: (toReturn: number) =>
    `Files to return: the seal was lifted and ${toReturn} files of its images are still in the quarantine. The images are shown again once whoever has the server has returned them (the README, Quarantine).`,
  /** [case.custody.lost], under a seal for good in force, and after a lifted seal. */
  custodyLost: (lost: number, inForce: boolean) =>
    inForce
      ? `Files lost: ${lost}. They were found in neither the image store nor the quarantine and are recorded as lost; there is nothing to move, hand over or destroy for them.`
      : `Files lost: ${lost}. Their images cannot be shown again; their author was told so.`,
} as const;

/**
 * 3d (design, sections 8 and 8.4): the console's words of what a program does and of the edge's purge, each under the
 * design's key. Task 3 brings the four lines of the edge's purge; every number is EDGE_WORDS', never typed, and the time
 * is the answer's, printed by the screen with bothTimes.
 */
export const AUTOMATION_WORDS = {
  /**
   * [case.purge.accepted], [case.purge.failed], [case.purge.off] and [case.purge.pending]: beside each image of a case
   * that stopped being public, and for each image of an order's disabled item, from the newest outbox row's outcome.
   */
  purge: (outcome: EdgePurgeView["outcome"], at: string): string => {
    switch (outcome) {
      case "accepted":
        return `Edge copy: purge accepted at ${at}.`;
      case "failed":
        return `Edge copy: purge failed. A copy may have been served for up to ${EDGE_WORDS.edgeMinutes} minutes after the measure; the operator is alerted.`;
      case "off":
        return `Edge copy: no purge (off): a copy may be served for up to ${EDGE_WORDS.edgeMinutes} minutes.`;
      case "pending":
        return "Edge copy: purge not sent yet.";
    }
  },
} as const;

/**
 * 3d Task 2 (design, sections 8.2, 8.5 and 8.7): the console's words of the release, each under the design's key
 * (`what` is [release.what]). Every number is printed from the answer or from the contracts' constants, never typed;
 * every time is the database's instant, printed by the screen with bothTimes. An authority's reference and a leave's are
 * an outsider's text, drawn framed, never in a label's place.
 */
export const RELEASE_WORDS = {
  title: "Release",
  /** The block's labels and values (8.5's table). */

    answeredAt: { label: "Assessed on", none: "no answer" },
    handedOverAt: { label: "Files handed over on", none: "nothing was handed over" },
    leave: { label: "Leave or instruction to destroy", none: "none recorded", from: { authority: "from the authority", court: "from a court" } as Record<string, string> },
    leaveReference: { label: "Its reference", none: "none recorded" },
    leaveDay: { label: "Its day", none: "none recorded" },
    tell: {
      label: "The author may be told",
      atOnce: "at once",
      untold: (until: string | null) => `not yet: the leave is recorded as not to be told to the person, ${until === null ? "with no end recorded" : `until ${until}`}`,

export const COMPOSER_WORDS = {

  sealSettled: "The numbers, the sentence about posts their author had deleted, and whether the seal changes anything are settled when the seal is recorded: the statement its author gets holds them as they are then.",
} as const;

/**
 * The shared codes a staff route may also answer, and the console's own: a network failure, an answer its schemas refuse,
 * a browser prompt that did not finish, step-up options that bind something other than the action the person chose, and
 * sign-in or enrolment options whose challenge is not one of that ceremony's.
 */
const OTHER_MESSAGES: Record<string, string> = {
  challenge_expired: "That took too long. Try again.",
  rate_limited: "Too many attempts. Wait a while, then try again.",
  invalid_request: "Some details are missing or invalid.",
  not_found: "That no longer exists.",
  csrf_failed: "This request could not be verified. Reload the page and try again.",
  service_unavailable: "That could not be done right now. Try again in a moment.",
  internal: "Something went wrong on the server. Try again.",
  network: "The staff console's server cannot be reached. Check your connection and try again.",
  invalid_answer: "The server's answer could not be read. Reload the page and try again.",
  ceremony_cancelled: "Nothing was signed: the browser's prompt was closed or timed out. Try again.",
  key_already_registered: "This key is already registered for your staff account. Use another key.",
  ceremony_refused: "The browser refused to use a key here. Open the console at exactly the address in CONSOLE_ORIGIN, never at 127.0.0.1, and try again.",
  step_up_mismatch:
    "The confirmation could not be checked: the server asked your key to sign something other than this action, so your key was not asked. Reload the page and try again; if it happens again, tell the operator.",
  signin_mismatch:
    "The sign-in could not be checked: the server asked your key to sign something other than a sign-in, so your key was not asked. Reload the page and try again; if it happens again, tell the operator.",
  enroll_mismatch:
    "The registration could not be checked: the server asked your key for something other than a staff key's registration, so your key was not asked. Reload the page and try again; if it happens again, tell the operator.",
};

const FALLBACK = "Something went wrong. Try again.";

/** The console's words for a code; a code it does not know, a passkey code included, gets the plain fallback. */
export function messageFor(code: string): string {
  if (Object.hasOwn(STAFF_MESSAGES, code)) return STAFF_MESSAGES[code as StaffErrorCode];
  if (Object.hasOwn(MODERATION_MESSAGES, code)) return MODERATION_MESSAGES[code as ConsoleModerationCode];
  if (Object.hasOwn(OTHER_MESSAGES, code)) return OTHER_MESSAGES[code]!;
  return FALLBACK;
}

/** The code of anything a screen's action threw, or null: the console's errors carry one. */
export function codeOf(err: unknown): string | null {
  return err instanceof Error && "code" in err && typeof err.code === "string" ? err.code : null;
}

/**
 * The words for anything a screen's action threw: the console's errors carry a code, anything else is the fallback.
 * `words` gives a screen's own words for a code where the shared ones would say too little: which daily limit was
 * reached, or what a link that names nothing means on the form it was typed into.
 */
export function describeError(err: unknown, words: Record<string, string> = {}): string {
  const code = codeOf(err);
  if (code === null) return FALLBACK;
  return Object.hasOwn(words, code) ? words[code]! : messageFor(code);
}
